plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value, regardless of beliefs about others' bids. Bidding higher than value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities where you'd have won at a price below your value. Since my value is $20, bidding $20 truthfully maximizes expected profit by ensuring I only win when profitable (paying less than $20) and never overpay.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding above my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding below my value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to exploit and no information about others' bidding tendencies, truthful bidding at $29 maximizes my expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value of $45 ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so (value ≥ second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Therefore, truthful bidding is optimal.
